summary:
Ohio is a state within the United States; federal law and the federal document regime apply here and are carried at national level. What follows covers Ohio's own statutes, courts and agencies.

Erin In The Morning's Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map of July 2026 places Ohio in "The Worst States," a group of sixteen states forming the second-highest tier beneath the four states graded "Do Not Travel," under the map's national frame of "Worst Policies In Effect."

Ohio's facility law, Senate Bill 104, the "Protect All Students Act," was signed by Governor Mike DeWine on 27 November 2024 and took effect 25 February 2025. It requires every K-12 school and every college and university, public and private, to designate bathrooms, locker rooms, changing and shower rooms and overnight accommodations for the exclusive use of males or females on the basis of sex assigned at or near birth, and requires students to use the facilities matching their birth certificate. Single-occupancy restrooms with controlled use are exempt. The bill was signed out of public view over the objections of Democrats, teachers' unions and civil rights groups; its sponsor was Republican state Senator Jerry Cirino. The statute contains no enforcement mechanism.

State identity documents are being narrowed. Amendment of the gender marker on an Ohio birth certificate was barred under the 1987 precedent In re Ladrach, challenged by four transgender Ohioans in March 2018 and invalidated as unconstitutional by federal Judge Michael H. Watson in Ray v. McCloud in December 2020; corrections have been officially permitted since 1 June 2021, although some counties continue to refuse them. Transgender people can change name and gender on Ohio driver's licences by court order together with a Declaration of Gender Change signed by a physician, nurse practitioner, social worker, therapist or psychologist, and an X marker has been available since April 2022. In August 2026 the Bureau of Motor Vehicles announced rules allowing only male or female markers and requiring an exact-matching birth certificate or passport.

Care and sport are governed by HB68, the Saving Adolescents from Experimentation Act, which bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s and bars transgender girls and women from women's high-school and college sports. It passed on 13 December 2023, was vetoed by Governor DeWine on 29 December 2023, and was enacted by House override on 10 January 2024 and Senate override on 24 January 2024. A court blocked it in April 2024, allowed it to take effect in August 2024 after finding the regulation of transgender individuals a legitimate state interest, and the Ohio 10th District Court of Appeals re-enjoined it on 18 March 2025, with Attorney General Dave Yost vowing to appeal. The operative position on any given provision should be checked before relying on it.

Protection is patchy. Ohio statutes do not address discrimination on account of gender identity, but gender-identity discrimination in state employment has been barred by executive order since 19 December 2018, and the Sixth Circuit held on 7 March 2018 that discrimination on the basis of transgender status is sex discrimination under Title VII. Thirty-three Ohio cities and counties have ordinances barring gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations.
tangentialFactors:
Ohio's placement is one tier below the four states graded "Do Not Travel" in the July 2026 assessment. The tiering reflects statutory text and its status in litigation rather than any measured incident rate, and the sixteen-state group is a count of jurisdictions, not a per-capita measure of risk.

Ohio's facility law carries no criminal penalty and no enforcement mechanism, which distinguishes it from the felony bathroom regimes that sit at the top of the same assessment. Exposure under Senate Bill 104 is therefore institutional: refusal by a school or college to permit facility use, with no stated penalty attached to the designation duty itself.

Trans civic participation has been targeted. In January 2024 transgender candidate Vanessa Joy was stripped from the ballot for failing to disclose her deadname under a seldom-enforced disclosure law, and three of four transgender state-office candidates that cycle were challenged or disqualified.

House Bill 8, signed 8 January 2025, requires educators, counselors and other school staff to out LGBTQ students to parents and bans "sexual content," including undefined "gender ideology," from kindergarten through third-grade curriculum with a parental opt-out.

Ohio recognises marriage regardless of the spouses' sex, as it has since the Supreme Court's ruling of 26 June 2015 in Obergefell v. Hodges, which invalidated Ohio's 2004 Defense of Marriage Act and the 2004 Issue 1 constitutional amendment. A trans visitor in what would be locally classed as a same-sex relationship can marry in Ohio and have that marriage recognised.

Proposed adult-care rules issued in January 2024 would have required perpetual psychiatric counseling, an ongoing endocrinologist relationship, bioethicist approval and 30-day reporting of gender dysphoria; they were dropped in February 2024 and are not in force.
localsOnly:
Ohio has no state statute barring discrimination on account of gender identity in private employment, housing or public accommodations. The protections residents actually hold come from a 19 December 2018 executive order covering state employment and from municipal and county ordinances: 33 Ohio cities and counties bar gender-identity discrimination across employment, housing and public accommodations.

There is no state conversion-therapy law after bills failed in 2013, 2015, 2020 and 2021. Several municipalities ban the practice for minors, among them Cincinnati in December 2015, Toledo, Columbus, Dayton and Athens in 2017, Lakewood and Kent in 2018, and Cleveland, Cleveland Heights, Akron and Reynoldsburg in 2022.

Changing the gender marker on an Ohio driver's licence requires a court order plus a Declaration of Gender Change signed by a physician, nurse practitioner, social worker, therapist or psychologist; an X option has existed since April 2022. The Bureau of Motor Vehicles' August 2026 announcement restricts markers to male or female with an exact-matching birth certificate or passport. Birth-certificate corrections have been permitted since 1 June 2021 following Ray v. McCloud, but practice varies: some counties continue to refuse corrections.

House Bill 8, in force from 8 January 2025, obliges school staff to disclose a student's LGBTQ status to parents and removes "gender ideology" from the kindergarten to grade three curriculum, with a parental opt-out for the remaining material.
outOfScopeNotes:
The operative status of HB68 is unresolved in the sources: the 10th District Court of Appeals re-enjoined it on 18 March 2025 and the attorney general announced an appeal, but no later ruling is sourced. Whether the care ban or the sports ban is currently enforceable should be verified before travel or enrolment.

Senate Bill 104 contains no enforcement mechanism, and the sources document no Ohio arrest, citation or reported case brought under it. How schools and universities apply the birth-certificate designation in practice, and whether complaints procedures exist, are not sourced.

The Bureau of Motor Vehicles' August 2026 marker rules are reported as an announcement. The final rule text, its effective date, and whether it has been challenged in court are not sourced.

County-level refusal to correct birth-certificate gender markers is reported as continuing after June 2021, but which counties, on what stated grounds, and with what remedy are not sourced.

The July 2026 risk map's tiering methodology is not set out in the sources beyond the tier labels, so the basis on which Ohio was separated from the four "Do Not Travel" states is unresolved.

Whether any replacement regulation for adult gender-affirming care followed the withdrawal of the January 2024 rules in February 2024 is not sourced.
